text.content:
Most attempts to Embrace a werewolf fail outright and the Garou simply dies, spared by Gaia from a fate worse than death. Rarely, though, the Embrace takes hold. The result is an Abomination: a vampire-werewolf hybrid, a thing that should not exist, cut away from the world's soul and denied the great cycle of life it was born into. Despair and suicide claim more Abominations than any Kindred or Garou hunter ever will. These are meant to be vicious, powerful, and above all rare antagonists — the appearance of one should be a shock, not a shrug.

Creation: The Last Gnosis Challenge

An Abomination is created exactly as any other vampire is (a normal Embrace), except that the dying/rising Garou may make one last Gnosis Challenge to try to escape the fate. No power short of divine intervention can affect this challenge.

  • Win: The victim dies quietly; her spirit passes on peacefully.
  • Tie: The Garou's spirit still passes on, but the death is bloody and agonizing.
  • Loss: The Garou becomes an Abomination.

What an Abomination Keeps

Like any other newly Embraced vampire, an Abomination learns three levels of Basic Disciplines and carries the weakness of whichever clan Embraced her (or she may be Caitiff). She can heal herself and boost her Attributes by spending blood, exactly like any other Kindred. That's where the benefits end.

What an Abomination Loses

  • Spirit connections wither immediately. She cannot increase her Gnosis, and can no longer heal naturally as a werewolf would — she must spend blood to heal, like a vampire.
  • Gifts and rites turn hostile. She may remember the Gifts and rites she knew in life, but using them no longer works the same way: they now only attract Wyrm-spirits, drawn by her new state as an unclean thing. If she wants to learn new Gifts or rites at all, she must learn them from Wyrm-spirits or Banes — foul, untrustworthy teachers with no interest in dealing honestly with her.
  • Blood, Gnosis and Rage no longer mix. An Abomination may not spend blood in the same turn that she spends Gnosis or Rage, or makes a Gnosis or Rage Challenge. The three pools interfere with each other too violently to use together.
  • Blood pool follows generation as normal for a vampire of her generation, same as any other Kindred.
  • Permanent, unliftable depression. An Abomination lives with a constant, debilitating depression that cannot be relieved by Willpower or any other means. She may never spend Willpower for retests.
  • Frozen psyche. She may never purchase further Humanity, Willpower, or Virtue Traits with experience, ever — her psyche is considered to be constantly eroding, and simply holding steady is the best she can hope for. Humanity often plummets quickly regardless, consigning most Abominations to death or the Beast before long.

What happens to an Abomination's spirit after Final Death — whether Gaia accepts her back after this living Hell, or whether she's cut off from the great cycle forever — is left deliberately unanswered.

Using Abominations at the Table

Abominations are not meant to be a playable character option or a common threat. Even the mightiest, most honored Garou elder becomes a pariah the moment she's Embraced, and is likely to have wrathful former packmates hunting her down to return her to the cycle. Reserve Abominations for rare, high-stakes Storyteller-character use.
